subject: Clarify auto-renew exemption & termination mechanics — Order Form v3
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form v3 — auto-renew opt-out request and notice window

Team / Samantha — attaching the latest draft (ACME_OrderForm_v3.pdf) and a proposed redline. Acme is pushing to keep the pilot flexible, and procurement asked to: 1) remove automatic renewal for the initial 12-month pilot; 2) reduce the termination notice window from 60 days to 30 days; and 3) include a termination-for-convenience option so they can wind down quickly if corporate priorities shift.

From a GTM perspective we want to keep the customer moving but we also need to protect revenue and uptime commitments for capacity that might be reserved. Laura — can legal advise whether we can: a) provide a one-time auto-renew exemption (no auto-renew for first term only), and b) accept a 30-day notice if we limit termination-for-convenience to pilots under $25k ARR or to non-reserved capacity only?

Samantha / Tom — can you confirm the expected spend for the first 12 months and whether any reserved capacity or dedicated instances are required? That will determine our exposure.

Next step: Laura, if you can share a short redline and a recommended guardrail (e.g., minimum notice or financial cap) we can send back to procurement this week and avoid a long legal loop.

Attachments: ACME_OrderForm_v3.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form v3 — auto-renew opt-out request and notice window

Agree with Mina — we should be pragmatic here. For pilots we can be flexible, but I prefer a mutual termination-for-convenience (so both sides retain symmetry) rather than Redwood unilaterally accepting their right to terminate on short notice without constraints.

If legal can propose: (i) a one-time no-auto-renew carveout for the initial 12-month term, and (ii) 30-day notice only if deal value < $25k or if we're on shared capacity (no dedicated GPUs), that would hit the right balance.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync if helpful.

— Aditya
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Jun 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form v3 — auto-renew opt-out request and notice window

Thanks for the background. I took a first pass — see attached redline (ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). High level comments: 

- Auto-renew: We can make the first 12-month term non-renewing (one-time opt-out) for pilots, provided the customer agrees to a modest notification that they will explicitly opt in to renew after the pilot. This should be limited to customers who do not request Dedicated/Reserved capacity.

- Notice window: Reducing to 30 days materially increases our operational and commercial risk if the customer consumes capacity that we could have reallocated. Recommend conditional 30-day notice: allowed only if total committed spend < $25,000 in the first 12 months AND they remain on shared hosted capacity. Otherwise retain 60-day notice.

- Termination for convenience: I recommend making termination for convenience mutual and limited to pilots under the same $25k threshold. If Acme requires unilateral termination for convenience (i.e., they can terminate for convenience but we cannot), that's asymmetric and I don't recommend it. 

- SOW / reserved capacity: If the SOW includes reserved GPUs or capacity commitments, we must not allow early termination without indemnity or pro-rated compensation for unused reserved capacity.

Next steps: Mina — confirm expected spend and whether they asked for reserved capacity. Samantha — please confirm spend projection (line item) and whether dedicated instances are in scope. If you confirm spend < $25k and no reserved capacity, I can produce a short clause insert to accomplish the one-time opt-out + 30-day conditional notice and mutual convenience termination.

Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (docx) — redline highlights and a one-paragraph fallback clause.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form v3 — auto-renew opt-out request and notice window

Thanks Mina / Laura — appreciate the fast turnaround. Quick clarifications from procurement: 

- Estimated spend for pilot: $18,500 total (first 12 months). No reserved capacity — this will be on shared hosted API.
- We want the ability to exit quickly if our roadmap shifts; mutual termination is fine. The one-time non-auto-renew carveout is acceptable.

Attached a signed SOW for the pilot scope (Signed_SOW_AcmePilot.pdf).

If Laura can produce the conditional clause we accept it and we'll route for internal sign-off.

Samantha Lee
Procurement Manager, Acme Corp

1) Acme confirms $18.5k spend and no reserved capacity — qualifies for conditional 30-day notice under the $25k cap.
2) Laura to produce a short clause: (a) first 12-month term one-time no-auto-renew; (b) 30-day notice permitted only if total spend < $25k AND no reserved capacity; (c) termination-for-convenience to be mutual for pilots under this threshold.

Laura — can you send the final one-paragraph insert by EOD tomorrow so I can push this through procurement and DocuSign?
